summary:
Jnr Astro  Mampare Outpost is a browser game where kids ages 7-12 run a small house in space. Inside the house stands Jnr, a junior astronaut. The player is boss of the house and must balance four things to keep him alive: Air, Protection, Food, and Warmth.

If you balance them, Jnr stands and smiles. If you forget one, he falls.

Players travel through three worlds  Gaborone, Mars, and Moon  and learn real trade-offs. On Mars, a dust storm forces you to sacrifice Warmth for Protection. On the Moon, a long freezing night forces you to prepare.

This answers the challenge  Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer  because kids do not just read about space, they train. They decide, fail, and try again.

details:
Jnr Astro - Mampare Outpost

Jnr Astro is a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer for kids aged 7-12. It turns space science into a game anyone can understand: Space is not hard. Space is just a small house.

You are the boss of a small house in space. Inside is Jnr, a junior astronaut. You must keep him alive for 30 sols by balancing 4 systems only: Air, Protection / Shield, Food, and Warmth.

If you balance them, Jnr stands and smiles. If you forget one, he falls. You count it on your fingers — no maths, no formulas, just balance.

How it works:
You play in 3 worlds. Gaborone teaches Sharing — like sharing water and power at home. Mars teaches Sacrifice — a dust storm hits like load shedding; you must choose what to protect. The Moon teaches Preparation — a long freezing night like winter; you must prepare before it comes.

There is no safe choice. If you push Protection up, Warmth goes down. If you push Food up, Air and Power cost more. Every choice has a cost, just like a real mission.

Impact:
Kids in Botswana and around the world learn that everything in space — and on Earth — is finite. If we don't balance, we will cease to exist. Balancing is a small price to pay for salvation. The game removes the fear that space is hard and teaches teamwork, sharing, and planning in plain language.

Tools and Data:
Built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, hosted on Netlify, works in any browser with no download, no account, and no payment. The design uses real NASA science: DONKI space weather for solar storms, OSDR astronaut health research for how the body reacts in space, and Artemis and Mars mission concepts for habitats. The demo was made in Google Slides.

Creativity and Team Considerations:
Our team considered age, language, cost, and access. We made it simple for a 7-year-old, fun for a 12-year-old, free for any school, and usable on a cheap phone. It was designed in Gaborone, Botswana, for the world — made to be played in class, at home, or anywhere.
